Question 7 Series compared with parallel

Buzz Question 7
MC - 2 points
Type: MC
Score: 2
7) Trials 4 and 5 used the same coil, core, and two cells and cost the same amount, but the series build had a higher strength-to-cost ratio. Which statement explains the difference?
A

Series wiring adds the two cell voltages, so a larger current flows through the coil and the magnetic field is stronger.

B

Series wiring removes the coil resistance, so the field no longer depends on current.

C

Parallel wiring cancels the iron core, so the field weakens.

D

Parallel wiring reduces the number of turns in the coil.

Question 8 Why more turns did not double the strength

Buzz Question 8
MC - 2 points
Type: MC
Score: 2
8) From Trial 1 to Trial 2, lifting strength increased from 49 to 54 clips, but cost increased from 14.14 to 17.28. Why did the strength-to-cost ratio decrease?
A

The added wire raised cost proportionally more than lifting strength; its resistance also reduced current, limiting the strength gain.

B

Iron stops responding once a coil has more than 20 turns.

C

The second set of turns was wound backward, so it cancelled the first set.

D

Doubling turns automatically halves the battery voltage.

Defend the optimized motor with CER

10) Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion defending your optimized motor against the baseline. Cite the complete settings and performance values for both designs, calculate or report the improvement, and explain how magnetic torque, back EMF, friction or load, and the resource/current constraints shaped the redesign.
Always Grading feedback: Grade the baseline-to-optimized comparison, quantitative improvement, motor-physics reasoning, and constraint tradeoff. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
A

Full credit: Gives complete baseline and optimized evidence, a correct improvement comparison, explains the important motor relationships, and justifies a constraint-based tradeoff. Partial credit: Gives a supported improvement but incomplete settings, physics, or constraints. No credit: Provides no baseline comparison or unsupported optimization claims.
